chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two divorces during the waiting period, then she contracted a temporary marriage (mut'ah). Is she permissible to her first husband after that? He said: No, until she marries another man.
ai.seo_question: Does a temporary marriage count as the second marriage required for a woman to become permissible to her first husband after two divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the mechanism of *tahlil* (restoration of marriage) by establishing that a temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) suffices as the intervening marriage required after two divorces, provided the conditions of the contract are met. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the form of the second marriage, distinguishing it from the stricter requirement of a permanent marriage in some other schools. The ruling underscores the importance of the actual consummation or valid contract of the second spouse to break the bond before the first husband can remarry her.
